claim: A dbus-daemon configured as type=session sets DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS (and DBUS_STARTER_BUS_TYPE=session) in the environment of clients it activates; the system bus address is normally well-known anyway
stance_target: system services cannot assume DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS: it is only set inside the session bus's activation environment
quoted_support: If the well-known type of the message bus is "session", then the DBUS_STARTER_BUS_TYPE environment variable will be set to "session" and the DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS environment variable will be set to the address of the session bus.

claim: The recommended session-bus topology is one bus per (user, machine) pair, shared between that user's login sessions
stance_target: per-user D-Bus reachability model: one session bus per user per host, shared across that user's sessions
quoted_support: recommend using a separate session bus per (user, machine) pair

claim: The per-user D-Bus service directory is resolved from $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dbus-1/services when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set
stance_target: user-session D-Bus service discovery depends on the user's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, which a system service does not have
scope_conditions: dbus-daemon service activation, systems with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR set
quoted_support: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dbus-1/services, if XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set (see the XDG Base Directory Specification for details of XDG_RUNTIME_DIR)

claim: The well-known session bus defaults to a fully permissive policy: any connection may send/receive any message and request any well-known name, so it must not be exposed beyond the user's runtime directory
stance_target: session bus is not a security boundary; exposing it to other UIDs is unsafe — system-bus policy files are the correct cross-UID channel
quoted_support: The well-known session bus normally allows sending any message. ... The well-known session bus normally allows any connection to request a well-known name and ... The well-known session bus normally allows receiving any message, including ... messages sent by other connections.
